subject: RapidRetail: sustained inference latency + 5xx errors — exec triage & closure
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@rapidretail.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: support@rapidretail.com
Date: 2028-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production errors and severe latency — impact on checkout flows

Hi Mina / Dylan,

We started seeing a sharp spike in latency across our Redwood-backed inference calls around 08:45 PDT today — median p95 jumped from ~120ms to >2.3s and we've had ~8% 5xx rate for the last 25 minutes. This is breaking our checkout recommendation flow and causing increased cart abandonment.

We have attached a small sample of failing requests (rapid_retail_error_sample.log) and a timeline from our side. Can you confirm whether this is a service-side regression or something on our integration? This is high-impact for us; our ops and product teams are standing by.

Elena Morales
Head of Product Operations | RapidRetail
[Attachment: rapid_retail_error_sample.log (text), service-timeline-20280401.csv (csv)]

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@rapidretail.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-01T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and severe latency — impact on checkout flows

Thanks for flagging this, Elena — really sorry for the disruption.

Quick summary of immediate steps:
- I’ve kicked off an urgent triage and looped the on-call infra and account leads (cc’d).
- We’ll run a canary to isolate model vs runtime issues and share a fault timeline in 30–45 minutes.
- If we need to, we’ll failover traffic to a compatible model variant while we stabilize.

Action: Can you confirm if the failing requests in your sample include requests with long prompt sequences or unusually large batched payloads? That will help us narrow whether it’s a KV cache/batching edge case.

I’ll update you within 40 minutes with initial findings.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0179

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-01T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and severe latency — impact on checkout flows

Update from triage (initial):
- Observed elevated queueing on the serving pool for the model assigned to RapidRetail between 08:36–09:02 PDT. GPU utilization spiked to ~98% with batched sequences longer than expected.
- Error pattern: transient 504/522 gateway responses originating from the runtime's request dispatcher when backlog exceeded threshold.
- Mitigation applied at 09:30: temporarily reduced max batch size and increased worker count for the pool. That brought p95 down to ~380ms but a small 5xx tail persisted.

Next steps:
1) Post-incident RCA to dig into why autoscaler didn't trigger aggressively (Jordan/David).
2) Short-term policy: pin RapidRetail to a higher-capacity pool while we complete RCA.
3) Customer communication: Mina to confirm the temporary failover and provide ETA for full RCA.

I'll attach the runtime logs to the internal thread.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runtime_dispatch_08xx.log (internal)]

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@rapidretail.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and severe latency — impact on checkout flows

Elena — quick update: we applied a temporary routing change at 09:30 PDT that moves traffic to a higher-capacity pool and reduced batch sizes; you should see error rates fall and latency improve. We expect full restoration within 2 hours while we conduct the RCA.

Immediate ask from you: please take no configuration action on your side. We will coordinate any client-side changes if needed.

Planned deliverables:
- Initial incident timeline and mitigation summary (this thread) — within 2 hours.
- Full RCA with corrective actions and ownership — by EOD 2028-04-07.
- Exec summary for your leadership and ours — by 2028-04-05.

Appreciate the patience and we’ll keep you updated.

— Mina

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-03T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: RCA draft and corrective action owners (RapidRetail)

Team — attaching the draft RCA and a short owner registry (also linked to the postmortem doc). Highlights:
- Root cause: autoscaler decision latency + a spike in unusually long prompt sequences from RapidRetail that increased batch assembly time. The combination led to sustained queueing and dispatcher timeouts.
- Corrective actions proposed:
  * Autoscaler telemetry: add backlog-rate delta metric and reduce trigger threshold (owner: Jordan Blake)
  * Model routing policy: auto-fallback to dedicated high-CPU pool when p95 > 800ms for 3 consecutive minutes (owner: Dylan Brooks)
  * Client guidance: recommend payload size limits and progressive batching (owner: Mina Haddad — coordinate customer comms)
  * Post-deploy tests: add synthetic long-prompt scenarios to the staging perf suite (owner: David Kim)

Please review owners and ETA estimates in the attached doc. We need exec sign-off on the routing policy change before we push it to prod.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Incident Response | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: postmortem-executive-summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: mina_haddad@redwood.com <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@rapidretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and severe latency — impact on checkout flows — RCA and next steps

Elena — attached is the finalized RCA and the executive summary. Key points for RapidRetail:
- What happened: orchestrated queueing due to combination of long-prompt traffic and a delayed autoscaler trigger.
- What we fixed: immediate pool failover on April 1; since then we’ve reduced default max batch size for your tenancy and implemented a temporary pin to a higher-capacity pool.
- Actions we will deliver:
  1) By 2028-04-14: integrator-level client guidance doc with recommended payload and batching patterns.
  2) By 2028-04-21: autoscaler threshold reduction + additional backlog-rate metric (Jordan owner).
  3) By 2028-04-28: staging perf tests covering long-prompt scenarios (David owner).

We acknowledge the impact and are offering a one-time credit to RapidRetail for April usage. Laura and I will coordinate the executive readout next week; happy to join your leadership call to walk through the mitigation and timeline.

Thank you for working through this with us — please let me know if you want a 30-minute walkthrough.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachments: postmortem-executive-summary.pdf, service-timeline-20280401.csv]
